articles.body: Over the past week, two separate client updates caught my attention for the same reason: both point away from the single-chat-box AI interface and toward something closer to a lightweight workspace manager. First, early UI sightings around Google Antigravity show work on curated plugin "Bundles" grouped by workflow or role, a dedicated agent creation screen (icon, name, goal, attached resources), and quota reset tokens alongside caching tweaks that reportedly stretched Neon usage by roughly 75% in five days. articles.title: NFS2ROOT: 12-Year-Old Linux Flaw Grants Root, No Login
articles.excerpt: Last updated: 28 November 2026. Verified against OpenSec's own NFS2ROOT disclosure as relayed by Cybernews and Sandbanks Digital's vendor-patch summary; seeHow this was checked. A bug that's been sitt…
articles.body: Last updated: 28 November 2026. Verified against OpenSec's own NFS2ROOT disclosure as relayed by Cybernews and Sandbanks Digital's vendor-patch summary; see How this was checked . A bug that's been sitting in the Linux kernel's built-in NFS server since 2014 just got a name, a working exploit, and a 9.8 CVSS score. CVE-2026-99362 — nicknamed NFS2ROOT by the security firm OpenSec — lets an attacker send a single crafted request to any exposed NFS server and walk away with a root shell. No login, no account, no user interaction. If a server is reachable on the right port and running the right NFS version, that's the whole prerequisite list.

articles.title: Streaming is where most OpenAI-compatible endpoints quietly break
articles.excerpt: A demo tells you a gateway works. It shows words appearing in a terminal, which is exactly the case where everything is already warm, the upstream is healthy, and nothing is queued. Production is the…
articles.body: A demo tells you a gateway works. It shows words appearing in a terminal, which is exactly the case where everything is already warm, the upstream is healthy, and nothing is queued. Production is the other case. The measure that matters is not total latency, it is time to first token (TTFT), and it is also the measure that aggregators most often ruin without noticing. Here is what we look at across 109 upstream models, and the failure modes that hide behind a 200. The four shapes of "streaming" Real streaming. Upstream emits deltas as it generates; the gateway forwards each SSE frame as it arrives. TTFT tracks the upstream's TTFT plus routing overhead. Buffered streaming. The upstream streams, the gateway collects, and then replays the whole answer as a stream of chunks.

articles.title: 8 Classic PlayStation Games That Are Barely Playable Today
articles.excerpt: From Tomb Raider to Silent Hill, eight classic PlayStation games whose tank controls, cameras, or lost code make them hard to play today
articles.body: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.

articles.title: Dropping missiles from orbit? 2 European companies sign agreement to study the idea
articles.excerpt: Atmos Space Cargo will fly its first Phoenix cargo-return capsule on SpaceX's Bandwagon 3 rideshare mission, which is scheduled to launch this spring.
articles.body: A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration.
